correctness.rationale: The polytope is the unit cube with a single positive normal halfspace cap in any d≥2 and T>0, so it is full dimensional and has exactly two possible vertex types: retained Boolean vertices S with a(S)≤T, and cut-edge vertices along edges from feasible S (a(S)<T) to infeasible S∪{i} (a(S)+a_i>T). Every retained Boolean vertex has an exclusive strict sign orthant of inward directions; for each absent singleton a_i>T, the new cut vertex on its edge from the all-negative corner requires another disjoint cone with u_j>0 (j≠i) and a·u<0, which forces u_i<0 and is incompatible with all kept orthants and other such cut vertices. This supplies |V|+|J| independent fractional weight lower bounds. Explicit directions u^S use one coordinate −2A/a_r and appropriate remaining signs (and u^∅ all plus), while absent singleton directions w^i have a large negative i-th coordinate; each strictly enters all active facets of every vertex. Thus the ordinary upper bound matches the fractional lower bound. Ties are covered by weak retained-vertex and strict edge crossing inequalities; cancellation of singleton thresholds gives d+1+#{|S|≥2,a(S)≤T}. Reconstructed rational cut-edge lists and independent strict active-normal checks for six examples including tied thresholds verified coverage; the proof, not these bounded checks, covers arbitrary real weights and all d.
residual_risks: Finite rational checks cannot verify all real weights.
The vertex-to-full-boundary extension uses standard polytope face incidence; no argument is offered for multiple cuts.

source_inspections.title: Fractional illumination of convex bodies

value.rationale: This theorem gives a dimension-uniform, complete, exact law for both ordinary and fractional illumination of a geometrically natural anisotropic single-facet perturbation of the cube, with all tied thresholds. The extra cut-edge witness shows retained cube vertex counting can be false (weights (3,1,1), T=5/2 give I=5, not 4), and singleton cancellation yields a sharp subset-sum staircase. It supplies many exact real convex-body illumination cases beyond upper-bound-only results and has a clear role in understanding fractional integrality and hypercube perturbations.
residual_risks: Single positive-normal cap only; counting feasible subsets may be computationally hard for varying d, and no polynomial algorithm is claimed.

limitations: Only one strictly positive-normal cap, not simultaneous cuts or arbitrary perturbations.
Exact formula is a subset-sum count and not claimed to admit a polynomial-time algorithm as dimension grows.
